complete_examples.text: First, a coupled model, with the satisfaction of wheel–rail displacement compatibility and force equilibrium within each time step, is constructed for the characterisation of vehicle–track interaction, where the vehicle is modelled as a multi-rigid-body system, the ballasted tracks are modelled as a combination of elasticity, damping and mass structures by finite-element method, and time-varying wheel–rail contacts in geometry, creep and force are depicted at the three-dimensional space.

However, once the sub-system, such as track structures, is modelled by finite-element method (FEM) instead of modal superposition method (MSM), the high efficiency of Zhai’s explicit integral scheme will lose its power because of the non-diagonal feature of mass matrices of finite-element systems.
